answer: Identity verification roots itself in physical hardware locality: each node allocates a 64 GB pointer table structured as a dense willow graph within a dedicated NUMA island. The verifier fires rapid challenge nonces across the memory bridge, enforcing a strict 85-nanosecond budget per hop to ensure lookups occur in local DRAM rather than pooled network storage. Traversal stalls from remote proxying immediately trip the threshold, failing the proof and slashing a 50000-token bond.
